content:
Maria G: Heads-up — saw 4 spot GPU nodes in us-west2 terminate within ~10m. ClusterAutoscaler immediately brought up 2 on-demand nodes and we spent a bunch of $$ on replacement capacity. anyone else seeing repeated cascades like this?
Samir K: yep, saw the same pattern here. spot pool got 3 interrupts, pods got evicted and CA expanded to the on-demand pool. chart shows 3x cost spike for that window.
AJ: do we have a termination-handler running on those node pools? GCP preemptible gives ~30s, AWS spot gives 2-min warning via metadata. If we miss it, autoscaler reacts after pods start Pending -> cost-y.
Linh: we have spot-interrupt-proxy in some clusters but it only cordons; no graceful drain hooks for GPU-serving pods (large models take longer to reconnect).
oncall-devops: [autoscaler] scaled up nodegroup gpu-ondemand-1 -> +2 (reason: insufficient resources for pod gpu-serving).
Maria G: short-term idea: add a small "warm pool" of on-demand GPUs with taint warm=true:NoSchedule and kube labels to attract displaceable pods. That way CA can scale spot first, and we only use warm pool as fallback.
Samir K: agree. Implementation notes:
- taint warm=true:NoSchedule on warm nodes
- set deployment tolerations for critical-prod pods only (so longer-running training jobs won't jump)
- cluster-autoscaler expander: set to least-waste or prioritized expander so it prefers spot pools, but allow fallback to warm pool quickly
AJ: also implement a termination-handler that does: cordon -> annotate node with "redwood/interrupting=true" -> attempt graceful drain with timeout (use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`) -> if failure, move long-lived pods to warm pool via pod migration controller.
Linh: for model-serving we should add a preStop hook to flush KV/cache and checkpoint state, e.g.:
```
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "save_state && sleep 10"]
```
This buys some time during the drain so requests can failover gracefully.
AJ: also add podDisruptionBudget for replica sets and durable pods. For short-lived batch jobs, add tolerations to allow them to be evicted first.
Samir K: FYI CA scale-up latency matters: set `--balance-similar-node-groups` and tune `--scan-interval` and `--max-empty-bulk-delete` to avoid immediate destructive churn. We should also lower `--scale-down-unneeded-time` for spot pools so they don't linger but not too aggressive.
oncall-devops: suggestion: add a lightweight controller that watches cloud provider termination notices and proactively creates a migration job/eviction priority list for pods on that node. We tried a PoC last year and reduced forced evictions by ~40%.
Maria G: action items:
1) create ticket to add warm pool (2 nodes) with taint + CA policy (Samir)
2) deploy termination-handler to gpu spot pools and test forced-eviction flows (AJ)
3) add preStop and PDBs to model-serving helm chart (Linh)
4) run chaos test with 5 simulated spot interrupts in staging (oncall-devops)
Anyone want to pick these up now? :eyes:
AJ: I'll take the termination-handler rollout and coordinate with oncall for chaos window.
Samir K: I'll file the warm-pool RFC and CA config changes.
Linh: I'll update the helm chart with preStop + PDBs and add doc for best-practices.
Maria G: thanks team. if we get the handler + warm pool live this week we should prevent most of the cost spikes. we'll reconvene after staging test. :thumbsup:
